# Brand tempo: calm and static against punchy and drifting

The s01 cinematic title rendered twice from the same scene plan, with only motion_preferences in brand.json changed: tempo calm with a static camera on the left, tempo punchy with the recipe's camera drift on the right. The HyperFrames animation reads both settings frame by frame.

- Type: Tempo variation
- Skill: `magnifito-promo`
- Engine: `hyperframes`
- Output: 1920x1080, 6 s, silent
- Video: [`../videos/v01-tempo.mp4`](../videos/v01-tempo.mp4)

## Recreate it with Claude Code

Install the plugin (see the repository README), open this folder, and give Claude this prompt:

> Use the magnifito-promo skill to show the client how the brand motion settings change a film. Take the cinematic title from showcase/s01-cinematic-title and render it twice with HyperFrames: once with motion_preferences.tempo "calm" and camera_style "static" (calm/), once with tempo "punchy" and camera_style "subtle_drift" (punchy/). Change nothing else. Put the two renders side by side with mgvideo multicam and label each half with its settings in Geist from fonts/ (labels.svg).

## Recreate it by hand

From the repository root, one command renders this example exactly as committed:

```sh
npm run showcase -- v01-tempo
```

Or run the steps yourself from `showcase/v01-tempo/` (after `npm run build && npm link`):

```sh
mgvideo render calm --force
node collect-run.mjs calm/runs work/calm.mp4
mgvideo render punchy --force
node collect-run.mjs punchy/runs work/punchy.mp4
mgvideo multicam work/calm.mp4 work/punchy.mp4 --layout side-by-side -o work/side-by-side.mp4
node rasterize.mjs labels.svg work/labels.png 1920 1080
ffmpeg -i work/side-by-side.mp4 -i work/labels.png -filter_complex "[0:v][1:v]overlay=0:0,format=yuv420p[v]" -map [v] -an -c:v libx264 -crf 16 -preset medium work/tempo.mp4
```

The finished file is `work/tempo.mp4`. The config files in this folder are the inputs.
